title: Brown Butter Pecan Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Toasted pecans steeped in the dairy, browned butter whisked in, brown sugar instead of caster, extra toasted pecans; no vanilla.
summary: A richer version of our classic custard: toasted pecans are steeped in the dairy, browned butter is whisked in, brown sugar replaces caster sugar and more toasted pecans go in at the end.

ingredients.note: half steeped and discarded; nutrition counts all

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast and steep
steps.text: Toast half the pecans in a dry pan for about 2 min until slightly darker and nutty, chop them finely and add to the cream and milk heated to steaming. Cover off the heat and steep for 1 h.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Melt the butter in the light-coloured frying pan over medium heat and keep cooking, swirling, until it smells nutty and the solids turn golden-brown. Set aside; a pale pan lets you see the colour change.

steps.title: Mix the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks and brown sugar in the clean saucepan.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Strain the pecan dairy onto the yolks, pressing on the nuts before discarding them, then whisk in the brown butter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over medium-low heat until the thermometer shows 77-80 °C, then stir in the salt.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Sieve again, cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: While it churns, toast and roughly chop the remaining pecans and chill them. Add them in the final minute and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Scrape all the browned bits from the pan into the custard; they hold most of the flavour.
A common mistake is browning the butter too far until black; pull it off the heat when it is hazelnut brown.
Stir the container before serving if the nuts have sunk.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
